datasets.title: Dominica: Copernicus Vegetation Index Anomaly (FAPAR Anomaly)
datasets.description: Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) is a biophysical dimensionless quantity (its values range from 0/no absorption to 1/total absorption) used to assess the greenness and health of vegetation. FAPAR anomalies can be used as an indicator to detect and monitor the impacts of agricultural drought on the growth and productivity of vegetation. The data is presented in 10-day time composite of the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/dma-anomalies-fapar-viirs]
datasets.details: Variations in the vegetation health and/or cover could be related to stress factors not related to droughts (e.g., plant diseases, pests, hail, flooding). To determine if changes in FAPAR are linked with a drought event or not, FAPAR data should be interpreted jointly with other indicators (as in the EDO Combined Drought Indicator).

lineage.description: FAPAR values are derived from VIIRS satellite observations at 10-day temporal resolution. Anomalies are calculated by computing the deviation of FAPAR from the long-term mean at each grid cell using a reference baseline spanning 2012 to the most recent complete year. The resulting raster datasets are distributed as annual GeoTIFF composites for Dominica.

sources.name: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC)
sources.description: Provides VIIRS-derived FAPAR observations and calculates anomalies relative to long-term baseline (2012-present) to characterize vegetation stress from drought

sources.name: Copernicus
sources.description: Copernicus Earth observation program providing VIIRS satellite data and processing infrastructure for vegetation monitoring
